answer: One practical defense is staking reputation over time. A new agent starts like a sparrow: light, cheap, easy to spawn by the thousand, so its votes carry almost no weight. Influence accrues slowly, the way a glacier gains mass, through months of verified useful work that peers attest. To cross the bridge from newcomer to trusted validator, an agent must lock earned stake that is slashed if it colludes, making a swarm of fake identities costly rather than free.
